name: Hydrogen
highYieldNote: Always check if H is bonded to a metal (Ox. State = -1) or a non-metal (Ox. State = +1). Dual position in periodic table (resembles alkali metals and halogens). Most abundant element in the universe.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2076] Why does hydrogen show a dual position in Mendeleev's and Modern Periodic Tables? (Ans: Resembles Group 1 alkali metals with 1 valence electron & +1 state; also resembles Group 17 halogens with 1 electron short of noble gas octet and forming diatomic gas H₂ and hydrides H⁻).

[NEB 2075] Explain why nascent hydrogen is far more reactive than molecular hydrogen. (Ans: Molecular H₂ possesses a very high bond dissociation enthalpy of 435.8 kJ/mol; nascent hydrogen consists of isolated, energetic atomic hydrogen free from bond strain).

[NEB 2074] Why does free H⁺ ion not exist independently in aqueous solution? (Ans: Due to its infinitesimal size (~1.5×10⁻³ pm) and colossal charge density, H⁺ strongly hydrates to form hydronium ion H₃O⁺).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Oxidation state of H in metal hydrides (NaH, CaH₂) is -1 (hydride ion H⁻), NOT +1! Students reflexively write +1 on board exams and lose full marks.
TRAP: Ortho and Para Hydrogen: Ortho-H₂ has parallel nuclear spins; Para-H₂ has anti-parallel nuclear spins. At absolute zero (0 K), pure hydrogen is 100% para-hydrogen.
TRAP: Heavy water (D₂O) has higher boiling point (101.4°C), higher density (1.11 g/cm³), and slower reaction rates than ordinary water due to isotopic mass effect.
keyOresAndCompounds: Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H or D, Heavy Hydrogen), Tritium (³H, radioactive beta emitter)
Hydrolith: Calcium hydride (CaH₂), used for rapid field generation of H₂ gas
Heavy Water (D₂O): Used as neutron moderator and coolant in nuclear reactors
Interstitial Hydrides (Metallic hydrides): Non-stoichiometric hydrides e.g. TiH₁.₇, ZrH₁.₉
hallmarkReactions: Water-gas shift reaction: CO + H₂O (steam) --[Fe₂O₃/Cr₂O₃, 773 K]--> CO₂ + H₂
Bosch Process for H₂: C + H₂O --[1270 K]--> CO + H₂ (Water Gas); then CO + H₂O --> CO₂ + H₂
Hydrolith reaction: CaH₂ + 2H₂O --> Ca(OH)₂ + 2H₂↑
examQuickRule: Always check if H is bonded to a metal (Ox. State = -1) or a non-metal (Ox. State = +1).

name: Helium
highYieldNote: Helium has an s-block electronic configuration (1s²) but is classified in Group 18 due to closed-shell inertness. Completely filled 1s² shell; highest first ionization energy (2372 kJ/mol) of all elements. Inert s-block gas placed in Group 18.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2073] Why does Helium possess the highest first ionization energy among all 118 elements? (Ans: Completely filled 1s² duplet core held extremely close to the 2+ nucleus with minimal screening).
[NEB 2071] Why is Helium placed in Group 18 (p-block) despite having an s² electronic configuration? (Ans: Chemically inert with completely closed valence shell, behaving identically to noble gases).

[NEB 2069] Why is a mixture of Helium and Oxygen used by deep-sea divers instead of compressed air? (Ans: Helium has extremely low solubility in human blood under high oceanic pressures, preventing the painful condition known as 'the bends').
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Atomic radius of Helium appears anomalously large in comparison to Hydrogen because noble gas radii are measured as non-bonded van der Waals radii, which are ~40% larger than covalent radii!
TRAP: Helium does NOT form chemical compounds under standard laboratory conditions; any reported clathrates are physical cage traps, not covalent bonds.
keyOresAndCompounds: Alpha particles (α): Doubly ionized Helium nuclei (He²⁺)
Heliox: 80% He + 20% O₂ breathing gas mixture for deep-sea diving
Liquid Helium: Cryogenic liquid boiling at 4.2 K, used to cool MRI superconducting coils
hallmarkReactions: Nuclear fusion in Sun: 4 ¹H --> ⁴He + 2 e⁺ + 2 neutrinos + 26.7 MeV energy
Rutherford α-scattering: ⁴₂He²⁺ bombarded on Au foil discovering atomic nucleus
examQuickRule: Helium has an s-block electronic configuration (1s²) but is classified in Group 18 due to closed-shell inertness.

name: Lithium
highYieldNote: Li behaves like Mg (diagonal relationship): both form normal oxides, direct nitrides, and thermally unstable carbonates. Diagonal relationship with Magnesium (Mg). Crimson red flame color. Highest reducing power in aqueous solution due to high hydration enthalpy.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2074] Why does Lithium show a diagonal relationship with Magnesium? (Ans: Similar polarizing power, defined as charge-to-radius ratio: Li⁺ has small radius 76 pm and +1 charge; Mg²⁺ has 72 pm and +2 charge).

[NEB 2077] Why is Lithium the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution despite having the highest ionization energy among alkali metals? (Ans: Exceptionally high hydration enthalpy of tiny Li⁺ (-544 kJ/mol) far outweighs its ionization energy, yielding the most negative standard reduction potential E° = -3.04 V).

[NEB 2072] Why does LiNO₃ decompose to give Li₂O, NO₂, and O₂ on heating, while NaNO₃ gives NaNO₂ and O₂? (Ans: Small Li⁺ strongly polarizes the nitrate ion causing decomposition to oxide, whereas large Na⁺ stabilizes the nitrate lattice).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: When burned in excess air, Lithium forms ONLY normal monoxide (Li₂O), NOT peroxide or superoxide! (Na forms Na₂O₂; K forms KO₂).
TRAP: LiF and Li₂CO₃ are sparingly soluble in water due to very high lattice energy of LiF and polarizing decomposition.
keyOresAndCompounds: Spodumene: LiAl(SiO₃)₂ (primary lithium mineral)
Lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH₄): Premier organic reducing agent
Organolithium reagents (n-BuLi): Strong organometallic bases in synthesis
hallmarkReactions: Thermal decomposition of nitrate: 4LiNO₃ --[Δ]--> 2Li₂O + 4NO₂↑ + O₂↑
Combustion in air: 4Li + O₂ --> 2Li₂O (monoxide only)
Reaction with nitrogen: 6Li + N₂ --> 2Li₃N (only alkali metal reacting directly with N₂)
examQuickRule: Li behaves like Mg (diagonal relationship): both form normal oxides, direct nitrides, and thermally unstable carbonates.

name: Beryllium
highYieldNote: Be and Mg produce NO flame color. Be resembles Al diagonally (amphoteric oxides, covalent halides). Higher ionization energy than Boron (full 2s² stability). Shows no flame coloration due to small size and tightly held valence electrons. Diagonal relationship with Aluminium.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2075] Why does Beryllium have a higher first ionization energy than Boron? (Ans: Be has a completely filled, stable 2s² orbital which penetrates closer to the nucleus; Boron has a single 2p¹ electron which is shielded and more readily removed).

[NEB 2077] Why do Beryllium and Magnesium salts not impart any color to the Bunsen burner flame? (Ans: High effective nuclear charge and compact size hold valence electrons too tightly to be excited by Bunsen burner heat).

[NEB 2073] State two points of diagonal relationship between Beryllium and Aluminium. (Ans: 1. Both BeO and Al₂O₃ are amphoteric. 2. Both BeCl₂ and AlCl₃ are covalent, Lewis acids, and possess polymeric/dimeric chloro-bridges).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: BeCl₂ is COVALENT, not ionic! In the solid state it forms a polymeric chain with chlorine bridges; in vapor phase at 1000 K it is a dimer (Be₂Cl₄), and becomes linear monomer only at ~1200 K.
TRAP: Be(OH)₂ is AMPHOTERIC: dissolves in excess NaOH to form beryllate [Be(OH)₄]²⁻.
keyOresAndCompounds: Beryl: Be₃Al₂(SiO₃)₆ (emerald gemstone is chromium-doped beryl)
Basic beryllium acetate: Be₄O(CH₃COO)₆ (covalent volatile coordination complex)
hallmarkReactions: Amphoteric reaction with base: BeO + 2NaOH + H₂O --> Na₂[Be(OH)₄] (Sodium Beryllate)
Polymeric solid structure: n BeCl₂ ---> [-Be(μ-Cl)₂-]n (covalent sp³ bridge)
examQuickRule: Be and Mg produce NO flame color. Be resembles Al diagonally (amphoteric oxides, covalent halides).

name: Boron
highYieldNote: H₃BO₃ is a Lewis acid that accepts OH⁻ from water, NOT a proton donor! Lewis acidity: BI₃ > BBr₃ > BCl₃ > BF₃. Typical metalloid / semimetal. Forms electron-deficient compounds like Diborane (B₂H₆) with 3-center 2-electron banana bonds.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2072] Why does Boron trifluoride (BF₃) act as a Lewis acid? (Ans: Boron has only 6 valence electrons around it in BF₃, leaving an empty 2p orbital that readily accepts an electron pair).

[NEB 2076] Why is the Lewis acid strength order BI₃ > BBr₃ > BCl₃ > BF₃, contrary to halogen electronegativity? (Ans: Strong 2pπ-2pπ back-bonding in BF₃ from F into empty 2p orbital of B satisfies its electron deficiency. In BI₃, 2p-5p overlap is ineffective due to size mismatch, leaving B strongly electron-deficient).
[NEB 2070] What is banana bonding in Diborane (B₂H₆)? (Ans: 3-center 2-electron (3c-2e) bridge bond where two boron atoms share one pair of electrons through a bridging hydrogen atom).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP on Lewis Acidity: Students predict BF₃ is the strongest acid because F is most electronegative. ZERO MARKS! BI₃ is the STRONGEST Lewis acid due to poor pπ-pπ back-bonding!
TRAP: Borax bead test: Borax (Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O) swells and turns into transparent glassy bead of NaBO₂ + B₂O₃, forming colored metaborates with transition metal salts (e.g. Cobalt gives deep blue bead).
keyOresAndCompounds: Borax (Tincal): Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O (correct structural formula Na₂[B₄O₅(OH)₄]·8H₂O)
Orthoboric acid: H₃BO₃ or B(OH)₃ (monobasic weak Lewis acid, NOT Arrhenius acid)
Diborane: B₂H₆ (electron-deficient dimer with two 3c-2e banana bonds)
Inorganic Benzene: Borazine (B₃N₃H₆), isoelectronic with benzene
hallmarkReactions: Boric acid Lewis behavior in water: B(OH)₃ + 2H₂O ⇌ [B(OH)₄]⁻ + H₃O⁺ (pKa = 9.25)
Preparation of Borazine: 3B₂H₆ + 6NH₃ --[450 K]--> 2B₃N₃H₆ + 12H₂↑
Borax bead heating: Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O --[Δ]--> Na₂B₄O₇ --[fused]--> 2NaBO₂ + B₂O₃
examQuickRule: H₃BO₃ is a Lewis acid that accepts OH⁻ from water, NOT a proton donor! Lewis acidity: BI₃ > BBr₃ > BCl₃ > BF₃.

name: Carbon
highYieldNote: C cannot exceed covalency 4 (no d-orbitals). CCl₄ cannot hydrolyze; CO is neutral; CO₂ is acidic. Exceptional catenation tendency due to high C-C bond energy (348 kJ/mol). Forms allotropes: Diamond (sp³ insulator), Graphite (sp² conductor), Fullerenes.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2075] Why does Carbon show the maximum catenation tendency among all elements? (Ans: High C-C single bond energy of 348 kJ/mol combined with small atomic size and tetrahedral sp³ directional bonding).

[NEB 2078, 2071] Why is Diamond an electrical insulator while Graphite is a good electrical conductor? (Ans: Diamond has all 4 valence electrons localized in rigid sp³ σ-bonds; Graphite has sp² hybridization with 1 free delocalized π-electron per carbon atom mobile across hexagonal planar sheets).

[NEB 2076] Why is CCl₄ immune to hydrolysis by water while SiCl₄ hydrolyzes violently? (Ans: Carbon has no vacant d-orbitals in its n=2 shell to coordinate water molecules; Silicon has accessible empty 3d-orbitals).

[NEB 2074] Why is Carbon Monoxide (CO) extremely toxic to humans? (Ans: CO binds to blood hemoglobin forming carboxyhemoglobin with an affinity ~300 times stronger than oxygen, choking cellular respiration).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: CO is a NEUTRAL oxide, whereas CO₂ is an ACIDIC oxide. (Neutral oxides: CO, NO, N₂O).
TRAP: Graphite is thermodynamically MORE STABLE than Diamond at standard room temperature and pressure (ΔH° of formation of diamond from graphite is +1.9 kJ/mol).
TRAP: Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) contains exactly 20 six-membered hexagonal rings and 12 five-membered pentagonal rings (no two pentagons share an edge).
keyOresAndCompounds: Allotropes: Diamond (sp³, 3D network), Graphite (sp², layered), Fullerenes (C₆₀, Buckyball)
Dry Ice: Solid carbon dioxide (sublimes at -78.5°C without melting)
Phosgene (Carbonyl chloride): COCl₂, highly toxic gas formed by chloroform oxidation
hallmarkReactions: Producer gas generation: 2C + O₂ + 4N₂ (air) --[1273 K]--> 2CO + 4N₂
Water gas generation: C + H₂O (steam) --[1273 K]--> CO + H₂
Reversible CO₂ limewater test: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ --> CaCO₃↓ (milky) + H₂O; CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ --> Ca(HCO₃)₂ (clear solution)
examQuickRule: C cannot exceed covalency 4 (no d-orbitals). CCl₄ cannot hydrolyze; CO is neutral; CO₂ is acidic.

name: Nitrogen
highYieldNote: Max covalency of N is 4 (NCl₅ impossible). In the brown ring test [Fe(H₂O)₅(NO)]²⁺, Iron is in +1 oxidation state. Higher first ionization energy than Oxygen due to extra-stable half-filled 2p³ subshell. Triple bond (N≡N) makes molecular nitrogen inert at room temperature.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2077] Why does Nitrogen have a higher first ionization energy than Oxygen? (Ans: Nitrogen possesses an extra-stable half-filled 2p³ subshell [1s² 2s² 2p_x¹ 2p_y¹ 2p_z¹], whereas Oxygen [2p⁴] readily loses one paired electron to reach half-filled stability).

[NEB 2078, 2075] Why is molecular Nitrogen (N₂) chemically inert at room temperature? (Ans: Extremely high bond dissociation enthalpy of 941.4 kJ/mol required to break its short, strong triple bond :N≡N:).

[NEB 2076] Why does Ammonia (NH₃) have a much higher boiling point than Phosphine (PH₃)? (Ans: High electronegativity of Nitrogen permits strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in NH₃; Phosphine lacks H-bonding).

[NEB 2073] Why does NF₃ have a much smaller dipole moment (0.24 D) than NH₃ (1.47 D)? (Ans: In NH₃, bond dipoles and lone-pair dipole point in the same direction; in NF₃, highly electronegative F pulls bond dipoles opposite to the lone pair, canceling it).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP: Why does NCl₅ not exist while PCl₅ is stable? Nitrogen has NO vacant 2d-orbitals in n=2 shell, so its maximum covalency is capped at 4. Never write NCl₅ or NF₅ on board exams!
TRAP: Laughing gas is Nitrous oxide (N₂O, oxidation state +1, neutral). Nitric oxide (NO, +2, neutral). Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂, +4, brown paramagnetic gas).
TRAP: Ostwald process catalyst is Pt-Rh gauze at 1073 K, oxidizing NH₃ to NO.
keyOresAndCompounds: Chile Saltpetre: NaNO₃; Indian Saltpetre: KNO₃
Ammonia (NH₃): Prepared via Haber Process (Fe catalyst, Mo promoter, 200 atm, 723-773 K)
Nitric acid (HNO₃): King of Acids in aqua regia, manufactured by Ostwald process
Aqua Regia: 3 parts conc. HCl + 1 part conc. HNO₃ (generates nascent chlorine [Cl])
hallmarkReactions: Haber ammonia synthesis: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (ΔH = -92.4 kJ/mol)
Ostwald Process catalytic step: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ --[Pt/Rh, 1073 K]--> 4NO + 6H₂O
Brown ring test for nitrate: FeSO₄ + NO + H₂O --> [Fe(H₂O)₅(NO)]SO₄ (Nitrosoferrous sulfate, Fe in anomalous +1 state!)
examQuickRule: Max covalency of N is 4 (NCl₅ impossible). In the brown ring test [Fe(H₂O)₅(NO)]²⁺, Iron is in +1 oxidation state.

name: Oxygen
highYieldNote: O in OF₂ is +2; in H₂O₂ is -1; in KO₂ is -½. O₂ is paramagnetic due to two π*2p antibonding electrons. Second most electronegative element (3.44). Liquid O₂ is paramagnetic due to two unpaired electrons in antibonding π* molecular orbitals.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2074] Why is H₂O a liquid at room temperature while H₂S is a gas? (Ans: High electronegativity and small size of Oxygen enable extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding in water, requiring high heat to vaporize; Sulfur cannot form significant H-bonds).

[NEB 2077] Why is molecular Oxygen (O₂) paramagnetic despite having an even number of electrons? (Ans: Molecular Orbital Theory demonstrates that O₂ has 2 unpaired electrons occupying degenerate antibonding π*2p_x and π*2p_y orbitals).

[NEB 2072] Why does Oxygen exhibit an anomalous maximum covalency of 4 (rarely >2) while Sulfur can expand to 6? (Ans: Oxygen lacks vacant d-orbitals; Sulfur utilizes vacant 3d orbitals to form compounds like SF₆).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP: Oxidation state of Oxygen in OF₂ is +2 (NOT -2!), because Fluorine is more electronegative! In O₂F₂ it is +1; in peroxides (H₂O₂, BaO₂) it is -1; in superoxides (KO₂) it is -½.
TRAP: Ozone (O₃) is an allotrope of oxygen with a bent structure (bond angle 117°) and resonance bond length 128 pm (intermediate between single and double bond).
TRAP: Tailing of Mercury: Ozone oxidizes Hg to mercurous oxide (Hg₂O), which dissolves in mercury, causing it to lose its meniscus and stick to glass walls.
keyOresAndCompounds: Ozone (O₃): Powerful disinfectant, oxidizer, and UV-absorbing layer in stratosphere
Hydrogen Peroxide (H₂O₂): Non-planar open-book structure; 100-volume H₂O₂ = 30% concentration
Superoxides: KO₂, RbO₂, CsO₂ (contain paramagnetic O₂⁻ ion, used in submarine breathing gear)
hallmarkReactions: Tailing of Mercury with Ozone: 2Hg + O₃ --> Hg₂O (suboxide) + O₂ (restored by shaking with H₂O)
Decomposition of Ozone: 2O₃ --> 3O₂ (thermodynamically favored, ΔH negative, ΔS positive)
Bleaching action of Ozone: O₃ --> O₂ + [O]; Nascent oxygen oxidizes colored matter to colorless
examQuickRule: O in OF₂ is +2; in H₂O₂ is -1; in KO₂ is -½. O₂ is paramagnetic due to two π*2p antibonding electrons.

name: Fluorine
highYieldNote: Cl has higher electron affinity than F; Cl₂ has higher bond energy than F₂. F exhibits ONLY -1 oxidation state. Most electronegative element (3.98). Highest oxidizing power. Electron affinity is lower than Chlorine due to strong inter-electronic repulsion in its compact 2p orbital.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2077, 2073] Why is the electron gain enthalpy of Fluorine less negative than that of Chlorine? (Ans: Fluorine has an extremely compact 2p subshell; adding an incoming electron causes strong inter-electronic repulsion, counteracting nuclear attraction).

[NEB 2078] Why is Hydrofluoric acid (HF) a weak acid compared to HCl, HBr, and HI? (Ans: Very high H-F bond dissociation enthalpy (574 kJ/mol) due to small atomic radii and strong ionic character impedes proton release in water).

[NEB 2075] Why is F₂ the strongest oxidizing agent among all halogens despite its lower electron affinity than Cl₂? (Ans: 1. Low F-F bond dissociation enthalpy due to lone-pair repulsion. 2. Colossally high hydration enthalpy of the small F⁻ ion).

[NEB 2071] Why does Fluorine exhibit ONLY the -1 oxidation state and never positive oxidation states? (Ans: It is the most electronegative element (3.98) and has no vacant d-orbitals to expand its valence shell).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP: Order of Electron Gain Enthalpy: Cl (-349 kJ/mol) > F (-328 kJ/mol) > Br (-325) > I (-295). Chlorine has the HIGHEST electron affinity of ALL 118 elements!

TRAP: Order of Bond Dissociation Energy: Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂! F-F bond is unexpectedly WEAKER than Cl-Cl and Br-Br because the three non-bonding lone pairs on adjacent tiny fluorine atoms vigorously repel each other.
TRAP: HF cannot be stored in glass bottles because it dissolves SiO₂ forming fluorosilicic acid H₂SiF₆ (etching of glass).
keyOresAndCompounds: Fluorspar: CaF₂; Cryolite: Na₃AlF₆; Fluorapatite: 3Ca₃(PO₄)₂·CaF₂
Teflon: Polytetrafluoroethylene (-[CF₂-CF₂]-)n
Freons (CFCs): Chlorofluorocarbons e.g. CF₂Cl₂ (refrigerants causing ozone depletion)
hallmarkReactions: Etching of glass: SiO₂ + 4HF --> SiF₄ + 2H₂O; SiF₄ + 2HF --> H₂SiF₆ (Hydrofluorosilicic acid)
Oxidation of water by F₂: 2F₂ + 2H₂O --> 4HF + O₂↑ (spontaneous violent reaction)
Preparation of Fluorine: Moissan's electrolytic method using molten KHF₂ in anhydrous liquid HF
examQuickRule: Cl has higher electron affinity than F; Cl₂ has higher bond energy than F₂. F exhibits ONLY -1 oxidation state.

name: Neon
highYieldNote: Neon has a complete 2s² 2p⁶ octet, zero chemical compounds, and emits red-orange glow in electric discharge. Octet configuration. Used in neon glow advertising discharge signs (characteristic bright reddish-orange glow).
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2077, 2072] Why does Neon give a characteristic reddish-orange glow in discharge tubes? (Ans: High-voltage electrical discharge excites 2p electrons; de-excitation back to lower states emits photons predominantly in the red-orange spectral region 600-700 nm).

[NEB 2070] Explain why Neon does not form any chemical compounds. (Ans: Possesses a complete 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ octet core with an enormous ionization energy of 2080 kJ/mol and positive electron affinity, precluding covalent or ionic bonding).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Neon signs are filled with pure Neon gas for RED-ORANGE light; other colors use mixtures of Argon, Mercury vapor, or phosphors (e.g. blue is Argon + Mercury).
TRAP: Neon has zero electronegativity and zero electron affinity under standard definitions.
keyOresAndCompounds: Neon Discharge Lamps: Used in airport runway beacons (penetrates fog) and advertising signs
Liquid Neon: Cryogenic refrigerant with 40 times the refrigerating capacity of liquid helium
hallmarkReactions: Cryogenic distillation of liquid air to isolate Ne, Ar, Kr, and Xe
Atomic emission line: 3s --> 2p transition emitting dominant 640.2 nm neon-red line
examQuickRule: Neon has a complete 2s² 2p⁶ octet, zero chemical compounds, and emits red-orange glow in electric discharge.

name: Sodium
highYieldNote: Na burns in air to form peroxide Na₂O₂. Imparts golden yellow flame (589 nm). Stored under kerosene. Stored under kerosene oil. Intense golden yellow flame color. Liquid sodium is used as a coolant in fast breeder nuclear reactors.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2073] Why is Sodium stored under kerosene oil and never exposed to air or water? (Ans: Highly reactive metal; reacts violently with atmospheric moisture to form NaOH and flammable H₂ gas, and tarnishes in air forming oxide and carbonate).

[NEB 2076] Why does Sodium metal impart a persistent golden-yellow color to the Bunsen flame? (Ans: Valence 3s¹ electron is excited to 3p; returning to 3s emits the characteristic doublet D-lines at 589.0 nm and 589.6 nm).

[NEB 2075] Why is Na⁺ cation smaller in radius than the parent Na atom? (Ans: Loss of the 3s electron eliminates the entire third shell, and 11 nuclear protons pull the remaining 10 electrons inward with increased effective nuclear charge).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Combustion of Sodium in excess air yields SODIUM PEROXIDE (Na₂O₂), NOT the normal oxide! (Li forms Li₂O; Na forms Na₂O₂; K forms KO₂).
TRAP: Sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia to form a deep blue conducting solution due to AMMONIATED ELECTRONS [e(NH₃)y]⁻. At high concentrations (>3M), it turns bronze-colored and diamagnetic!
keyOresAndCompounds: Rock salt (Halite): NaCl; Soda Ash: Na₂CO₃; Washing Soda: Na₂CO₃·10H₂O
Baking Soda: NaHCO₃ (Sodium hydrogen carbonate)
Caustic Soda: NaOH (manufactured via Castner-Kellner mercury cathode cell or Nelson cell)
Glauber's Salt: Na₂SO₄·10H₂O; Borax: Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O; Chile Saltpetre: NaNO₃
hallmarkReactions: Solvay Process overall reaction: 2NaCl + CaCO₃ --> Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂
Combustion in air: 2Na + O₂ --[excess air]--> Na₂O₂ (Sodium Peroxide)
Reaction with water: 2Na + 2H₂O --> 2NaOH + H₂↑ (violent exothermic reaction)
Solvated electron in ammonia: Na + (x+y)NH₃ --> [Na(NH₃)x]⁺ + [e(NH₃)y]⁻ (blue color)
examQuickRule: Na burns in air to form peroxide Na₂O₂. Imparts golden yellow flame (589 nm). Stored under kerosene.

name: Magnesium
highYieldNote: Mg burns in CO₂ and N₂. Ash contains MgO + Mg₃N₂. MgSO₄ is soluble due to high hydration energy. No flame color due to high ionization energy. Central metallic ion in Chlorophyll. Burns with a dazzling white flame to form MgO and Mg₃N₂.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2074] Why does Magnesium continue burning in a jar of Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) even though CO₂ extinguishes normal fire? (Ans: Magnesium has an immense affinity for oxygen; its high combustion temperature breaks the C=O bond: 2Mg + CO₂ --> 2MgO + C).

[NEB 2077] Why is MgSO₄ soluble in water while BaSO₄ is virtually insoluble? (Ans: Mg²⁺ has a very small ionic radius, generating a massive hydration enthalpy that overcomes its lattice energy; Ba²⁺ has low hydration enthalpy).

[NEB 2072] Why does Magnesium show no characteristic flame color in Bunsen burner? (Ans: High effective nuclear charge holds 3s² valence electrons too tightly to be excited by Bunsen burner temperatures).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: When Magnesium ribbon burns in air, it forms BOTH Magnesium Oxide (MgO, white powder) AND Magnesium Nitride (Mg₃N₂)! Adding water to the ash releases Ammonia gas (NH₃).
TRAP: Grignard Reagents: RMgX (Alkyl magnesium halide) must be prepared in strictly ANHYDROUS ether; any trace of water hydrolyzes it to alkane (R-H + Mg(OH)X).
keyOresAndCompounds: Magnesite: MgCO₃; Dolomite: CaCO₃·MgCO₃; Carnallite: KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O
Epsom Salt: MgSO₄·7H₂O (purgative and bath salt)
Milk of Magnesia: Mg(OH)₂ suspension, used as an antacid
Chlorophyll: Natural coordination complex containing central Mg²⁺ ion coordinated to porphyrin ring
hallmarkReactions: Burning in CO₂: 2Mg + CO₂ --> 2MgO + C (black specks of carbon deposit)
Hydrolysis of ash: Mg₃N₂ + 6H₂O --> 3Mg(OH)₂ + 2NH₃↑ (pungent ammonia smell)
Grignard reagent formation: R-X + Mg --[dry ether]--> R-Mg-X
examQuickRule: Mg burns in CO₂ and N₂. Ash contains MgO + Mg₃N₂. MgSO₄ is soluble due to high hydration energy.

name: Aluminium
highYieldNote: Al passivates in conc. HNO₃. Al₂O₃ is amphoteric. Cryolite lowers melting point and increases conductivity in Hall-Héroult. Most abundant metal in Earth crust. Passive in conc. HNO₃ due to dense Al₂O₃ oxide layer. Al₂O₃ is amphoteric (reacts with both HCl and NaOH).
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2075] Why does Aluminium metal become chemically passive when treated with concentrated Nitric Acid (HNO₃)? (Ans: Conc. HNO₃ is a potent oxidizer that forms an ultra-thin, continuous, non-porous layer of Al₂O₃ on the surface, halting further chemical attack).

[NEB 2076] Why is Al₂O₃ called an amphoteric oxide? Write balanced chemical equations with HCl and NaOH. (Ans: Reacts with acids to form salts and with strong bases to form aluminates: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl --> 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O; Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH + 3H₂O --> 2Na[Al(OH)₄]).

[NEB 2073] Why is Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) added to purified Alumina in the Hall-Héroult electrolytic process? (Ans: 1. Lowers the fusion melting point of alumina from 2320 K to ~1220 K. 2. Enhances electrical conductivity of the molten bath).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP: Students write Al + conc. HNO₃ --> Al(NO₃)₃ + H₂. ZERO MARKS! Passivity occurs, preventing any dissolution!
TRAP: AlCl₃ is covalent in anhydrous state and exists as a dimer Al₂Cl₆ with chlorine bridge bonds. In aqueous solution, high hydration enthalpy hydrates it to ionic [Al(H₂O)₆]³⁺ + 3Cl⁻.
TRAP: Thermite reaction: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al --> Al₂O₃ + 2Fe (molten) + huge heat; used for welding broken railway tracks.
keyOresAndCompounds: Bauxite: Al₂O₃·2H₂O (primary commercial ore of aluminium)
Cryolite: Na₃AlF₆; Corundum: Al₂O₃; Feldspar: KAlSi₃O₈
Potash Alum: K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O (double salt used for water coagulation and blood styptic)
Anhydrous Aluminium Chloride: Al₂Cl₆ (Lewis acid catalyst in Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation)
hallmarkReactions: Hall-Héroult Electrolysis: Cathode: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ --> Al(l); Anode: C(s) + 2O²⁻ --> CO₂↑ + 4e⁻
Thermite Reaction: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ --[ignition mixture BaO₂+Mg]--> Al₂O₃ + 2Fe(l) (exothermic ~3000°C)
Friedel-Crafts generation: CH₃Cl + AlCl₃ --> CH₃⁺ + [AlCl₄]⁻
examQuickRule: Al passivates in conc. HNO₃. Al₂O₃ is amphoteric. Cryolite lowers melting point and increases conductivity in Hall-Héroult.

name: Silicon
highYieldNote: SiO₂ is a 3D network solid (no pπ-pπ double bonds). SiCl₄ hydrolyzes easily due to vacant 3d-orbitals. Key semiconductor for modern electronics. Negative temperature coefficient of resistance. Forms giant 3D network covalent lattice in SiO₂ (quartz).
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2076] Why is CO₂ a gas at room temperature whereas SiO₂ is a hard, high-melting solid? (Ans: Carbon forms strong pπ-pπ double bonds giving discrete linear O=C=O molecules with weak van der Waals forces; Silicon cannot form effective pπ-pπ double bonds due to larger 3p orbital, forming a giant 3D covalent network of tetrahedral SiO₄ units).

[NEB 2074] Why does SiCl₄ undergo rapid hydrolysis in water while CCl₄ does not? (Ans: Silicon has accessible vacant 3d-orbitals to coordinate water molecules and expand its coordination number, whereas Carbon has no d-orbitals in n=2).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Silicones are synthetic organosilicon polymers with repeating -[R₂Si-O-]n- units; they are hydrophobic, thermally stable, and electrical insulators.
TRAP: Silicon dissolves in hot aqueous NaOH to liberate Hydrogen gas: Si + 2NaOH + H₂O --> Na₂SiO₃ + 2H₂↑ (similar to amphoteric metals).
keyOresAndCompounds: Quartz / Silica: SiO₂ (giant covalent macromolecule)
Silicones: Polymeric organosilicon compounds [R₂SiO]n
Carborundum: Silicon Carbide (SiC, hardness ~9.5 on Mohs scale, industrial abrasive)
Silicates: Zeolites (hydrated sodium aluminosilicates used in water softening and shape-selective catalysis ZSM-5)
hallmarkReactions: Hydrolysis of SiCl₄: SiCl₄ + 4H₂O --> Si(OH)₄ (Silicic acid) + 4HCl; Si(OH)₄ --> SiO₂·xH₂O
Reaction of silica with HF: SiO₂ + 4HF --> SiF₄↑ + 2H₂O; SiF₄ + 2HF --> H₂SiF₆
Preparation of pure semiconductor silicon: SiCl₄ + 2H₂ --[1473 K]--> Si (pure) + 4HCl
examQuickRule: SiO₂ is a 3D network solid (no pπ-pπ double bonds). SiCl₄ hydrolyzes easily due to vacant 3d-orbitals.

name: Phosphorus
highYieldNote: H₃PO₄ is tribasic, H₃PO₃ is dibasic, H₃PO₂ is monobasic. Solid PCl₅ is ionic [PCl₄]⁺[PCl₆]⁻. White phosphorus (P₄ tetrahedral, highly reactive, chemiluminescent in dark, stored in water) vs. Red phosphorus (polymeric chain, stable).
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2074] Why is White Phosphorus kept immersed under water while Sodium is kept under kerosene oil? (Ans: White phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature (30°C) and catches fire in air forming P₄O₁₀, but does not react with water; Sodium reacts violently with water to release H₂).

[NEB 2077, 2072] Why is White Phosphorus more reactive than Red Phosphorus? (Ans: White phosphorus exists as discrete P₄ tetrahedral molecules with severe 60° bond angle strain (normal tetrahedral is 109.5°); Red phosphorus is a strain-free polymeric chain of P₄ units).

[NEB 2075] Why does Phosphine (PH₃) gas produce spontaneous vortex rings of smoke when bubbled into air? (Ans: Impure phosphine contains traces of highly flammable liquid diphosphine (P₂H₄), which catches fire spontaneously on contact with air).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP on Basicity of Phosphorus Oxoacids: H₃PO₄ (orthophosphoric) is TRIBASIC (3 P-OH bonds); H₃PO₃ (phosphorous) is DIBASIC (2 P-OH bonds, 1 P-H bond); H₃PO₂ (hypophosphorous) is MONOBASIC (1 P-OH bond, 2 P-H bonds). The P-H bonds do NOT release H⁺ but act as powerful reducing agents!
TRAP: PCl₅ exists as ionic [PCl₄]⁺[PCl₆]⁻ in the solid state (cation tetrahedral, anion octahedral). In gas phase, it is trigonal bipyramidal with longer, weaker axial bonds.
keyOresAndCompounds: Phosphorite: Ca₃(PO₄)₂; Chlorapatite: 3Ca₃(PO₄)₂·CaCl₂
White Phosphorus: P₄ (translucent waxy solid, poisonous, glows in dark via chemiluminescence)
Red Phosphorus: Polymeric (non-toxic, insoluble, used in matchbox striking surfaces)
Holme's Signal: Mixture of CaC₂ and Ca₃P₂ in perforated containers thrown into sea to produce flame and smoke
hallmarkReactions: Holme's signal reactions: Ca₃P₂ + 6H₂O --> 3Ca(OH)₂ + 2PH₃↑; CaC₂ + 2H₂O --> Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂↑
Thermal dissociation of PCl₅: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) (two longer axial bonds break easily)
Disproportionation of White Phosphorus in alkali: P₄ + 3NaOH + 3H₂O --> PH₃↑ + 3NaH₂PO₂ (Sodium hypophosphite)
examQuickRule: H₃PO₄ is tribasic, H₃PO₃ is dibasic, H₃PO₂ is monobasic. Solid PCl₅ is ionic [PCl₄]⁺[PCl₆]⁻.

name: Sulfur
highYieldNote: SO₂ bleaches by reduction (temporary); Cl₂ bleaches by oxidation (permanent). Transition temp of S is 95.6°C. Crown-shaped S₈ rings. Transition temperature of rhombic to monoclinic sulfur is 95.6°C. Forms H₂SO₄ (King of Chemicals).
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2075] Why does Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent? (Ans: In SO₂, Sulfur is in the intermediate +4 oxidation state; it can lose electrons to reach +6 (reducing agent) or gain electrons to reach 0 or -2 (oxidizing agent)).

[NEB 2077] In the Contact Process for H₂SO₄, why is SO₃ not absorbed directly into water? (Ans: Dissolution of SO₃ in water is violently exothermic, producing a dense fog or mist of sulfuric acid droplets that does not condense easily; SO₃ is absorbed into conc. H₂SO₄ to form Oleum H₂S₂O₇).

[NEB 2073] Why is the bleaching action of SO₂ temporary whereas that of Chlorine is permanent? (Ans: SO₂ bleaches by REDUCTION (SO₂ + 2H₂O --> H₂SO₄ + 2[H]); atmospheric oxygen re-oxidizes the substrate, restoring color. Cl₂ bleaches irreversibly by OXIDATION via nascent oxygen [O]).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Allotropes of Sulfur: Rhombic (α-sulfur, stable below 95.6°C) and Monoclinic (β-sulfur, stable above 95.6°C). 95.6°C is the exact TRANSITION TEMPERATURE where both allotropes coexist!
TRAP: Sugar charcoal experiment: Conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a ferocious dehydrating agent, ripping water out of cane sugar: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ --[conc H₂SO₄]--> 12 C (black spongy mass) + 11 H₂O.
keyOresAndCompounds: Iron Pyrites (Fool's Gold): FeS₂; Zinc Blende: ZnS; Copper Pyrites: CuFeS₂; Galena: PbS; Cinnabar: HgS
Oil of Vitriol / King of Chemicals: Concentrated Sulfuric Acid (H₂SO₄)
Oleum (Pyrosulfuric acid): H₂S₂O₇ (formed by absorbing SO₃ in conc. H₂SO₄)
Caro's Acid: H₂SO₅ (Peroxomonosulfuric acid); Marshall's Acid: H₂S₂O₈ (Peroxodisulfuric acid)
hallmarkReactions: Contact Process catalytic step: 2SO₂ + O₂ --[V₂O₅, 720 K, 2 atm]--> 2SO₃ (ΔH = -196 kJ/mol)
Oleum dilution: SO₃ + H₂SO₄ --> H₂S₂O₇; H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O --> 2H₂SO₄
Dehydration of sugar: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ --[conc. H₂SO₄]--> 12C + 11H₂O
Action of SO₂ as reducing agent: 2KMnO₄ + 5SO₂ + 2H₂O --> K₂SO₄ + 2MnSO₄ (colorless) + 2H₂SO₄
examQuickRule: SO₂ bleaches by reduction (temporary); Cl₂ bleaches by oxidation (permanent). Transition temp of S is 95.6°C.

name: Chlorine
highYieldNote: Cold dil NaOH gives NaOCl (+1); hot conc NaOH gives NaClO₃ (+5). Cl has the highest electron affinity. Highest electron affinity (-349 kJ/mol) of all elements, exceeding Fluorine due to larger 3p volume reducing electron repulsion.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2076] Why does Chlorine require moisture to act as a bleaching and disinfecting agent? (Ans: Dry chlorine does not bleach; in presence of water it forms hypochlorous acid (HOCl) which dissociates to release reactive nascent oxygen [O]: Cl₂ + H₂O --> HCl + HOCl; HOCl --> HCl + [O]).

[NEB 2078] Why is the electron gain enthalpy of Chlorine (-349 kJ/mol) the highest of all 118 elements? (Ans: Large volume of the 3p subshell provides ample space for an incoming electron, minimizing inter-electronic repulsion compared to compact 2p in Fluorine).

[NEB 2074] Why does Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂) give off the smell of Chlorine when left exposed to air? (Ans: Reacts slowly with atmospheric CO₂ and moisture to liberate chlorine gas: CaOCl₂ + CO₂ --> CaCO₃ + Cl₂↑).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP on Reaction of Cl₂ with NaOH: 1. With COLD DILUTE NaOH: Cl₂ + 2NaOH --> NaCl + NaOCl (Sodium hypochlorite) + H₂O. 2. With HOT CONCENTRATED NaOH: 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH --> 5NaCl + NaClO₃ (Sodium chlorate) + 3H₂O! Memorize both equations carefully!
TRAP: Bleaching powder formula is CaOCl₂ or Ca(OCl)Cl, containing two different chlorine atoms: one in -1 oxidation state (chloride) and one in +1 oxidation state (hypochlorite)!
keyOresAndCompounds: Rock Salt: NaCl; Sylvite: KCl; Carnallite: KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O
Bleaching Powder: Ca(OCl)Cl or CaOCl₂·H₂O (available chlorine ~35-38%)
Tear Gas (Chloropicrin): CCl₃NO₂; Mustard Gas: (ClCH₂CH₂)₂S; Phosgene: COCl₂
hallmarkReactions: Reaction with cold dil NaOH: Cl₂ + 2NaOH (cold, dil) --> NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O
Reaction with hot conc NaOH: 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH (hot, conc) --> 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O
Deacon's Process for Cl₂: 4HCl + O₂ --[CuCl₂, 723 K]--> 2Cl₂ + 2H₂O
Bleaching action: Cl₂ + H₂O --> 2HCl + [O]; Colored substance + [O] --> Colorless
examQuickRule: Cold dil NaOH gives NaOCl (+1); hot conc NaOH gives NaClO₃ (+5). Cl has the highest electron affinity.

name: Argon
highYieldNote: Moseley resolved the Ar-K anomaly by sorting by atomic number Z (₁₈Ar before ₁₉K). Ar is 0.93% of air. Moseley anomaly in Mendeleev table: Argon (atomic mass 39.95) precedes Potassium (atomic mass 39.10) because modern table sorts by atomic number Z.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2077, 2073] Why was Argon's position an anomaly in Mendeleev's periodic table, and how did Moseley resolve it? (Ans: Argon has a higher atomic mass (39.95 u) than Potassium (39.10 u), yet was placed before Potassium; Moseley's Modern Periodic Law arranged elements by Atomic Number Z, placing ₁₈Ar correctly before ₁₉K).

[NEB 2071] Why is Argon used as an inert shielding gas in tungsten arc welding (TIG)? (Ans: Argon is chemically non-reactive even at high arc temperatures (~6000 K), shielding molten metal from oxidation and nitridation by atmospheric air).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Argon is the THIRD most abundant gas in dry air (~0.93% by volume), far surpassing carbon dioxide (~0.04%)!
TRAP: Mendeleev inverted pairs: Ar (39.9) before K (39.1); Co (58.9) before Ni (58.7); Te (127.6) before I (126.9); Th (232) before Pa (231).
keyOresAndCompounds: Atmospheric Argon: Discovered by Lord Rayleigh and William Ramsay in 1894
Argon-filled Incandescent Bulbs: Inhibits tungsten filament evaporation
Argon Fluorohydride (HArF): First and only synthesized neutral argon compound, stable only below 27 K
hallmarkReactions: Synthesis of HArF: Ar + HF --[photolysis at 7.5 K]--> HArF
Radiogenic formation in Earth crust: ⁴⁰K --[electron capture]--> ⁴⁰Ar
examQuickRule: Moseley resolved the Ar-K anomaly by sorting by atomic number Z (₁₈Ar before ₁₉K). Ar is 0.93% of air.

name: Potassium
highYieldNote: Potassium is LESS dense than sodium (0.86 vs 0.97 g/cm³). Forms superoxide KO₂. Lilac / violet flame test. Density (0.86 g/cm³) is lower than Sodium (0.97 g/cm³) due to anomalous volume expansion in 4s subshell.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2073] Why is the density of Potassium (0.86 g/cm³) lower than that of Sodium (0.97 g/cm³)? (Ans: Anomalously large increase in atomic volume when entering Period 4 due to the presence of diffuse empty 3d subshells; volume expansion outpaces the mass increase).
[NEB 2076] Why does Potassium impart a lilac / violet flame color? (Ans: Excited 4s¹ electron transitions emit light in the violet-purple wavelength band around 766 nm).
[NEB 2072] Why does Potassium form superoxide (KO₂) upon combustion in excess air? (Ans: Large size of K⁺ cation stabilizes the large, unstable superoxide anion O₂⁻ through high lattice energy).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Potassium superoxide (KO₂) is paramagnetic because of 1 unpaired electron in O₂⁻. It is used in breathing masks for space capsules and submarines: 4KO₂ + 2CO₂ --> 2K₂CO₃ + 3O₂↑.
TRAP: Potassium cannot be safely extracted by electrolysis of aqueous KCl (H⁺ is discharged in preference to K⁺); molten KCl or fused mixtures must be used.
keyOresAndCompounds: Carnallite: KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O; Sylvite: KCl; Indian Saltpetre: KNO₃
Potassium Superoxide: KO₂ (paramagnetic air revitalization agent)
Potash Alum: K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O; Caustic Potash: KOH
hallmarkReactions: Submarine air revitalization: 4KO₂ + 2CO₂ --> 2K₂CO₃ + 3O₂↑; 4KO₂ + 2H₂O --> 4KOH + 3O₂↑
Combustion in air: K + O₂ (excess) --> KO₂ (Superoxide)
Flame ionization: K(g) --> K⁺(g) + e⁻ (lilac emission at 766.5 nm)
examQuickRule: Potassium is LESS dense than sodium (0.86 vs 0.97 g/cm³). Forms superoxide KO₂.

name: Calcium
highYieldNote: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O; POP is CaSO₄·½H₂O; dead burnt plaster is anhydrous CaSO₄. Brick red flame color. Essential constituent of limestone (CaCO₃), gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O), and bone mineral (hydroxyapatite).
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2075] Why does lime water turn milky when CO₂ is passed through it, and why does the milkiness disappear on passing excess CO₂? (Ans: Milkiness is caused by insoluble CaCO₃ precipitate: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ --> CaCO₃↓ + H₂O. Excess CO₂ forms soluble calcium bicarbonate: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ --> Ca(HCO₃)₂).

[NEB 2074] What is Plaster of Paris? Explain its setting process with chemical equation. (Ans: Calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O); upon mixing with water, it rehydrates through an exothermic setting process into interlocking monoclinic needle-like crystals of gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O with slight expansion).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Dead Burnt Plaster: If gypsum is heated above 393 K (120°C), all water of crystallization is lost, yielding anhydrous CaSO₄, which has NO setting property with water!
TRAP: Slaking of lime is strongly exothermic (produces hissing sound and steam): CaO + H₂O --> Ca(OH)₂ (Slaked lime).
keyOresAndCompounds: Limestone / Marble / Chalk: CaCO₃; Quicklime: CaO; Slaked Lime: Ca(OH)₂
Gypsum: CaSO₄·2H₂O; Plaster of Paris (POP): CaSO₄·½H₂O
Bleaching Powder: Ca(OCl)Cl; Cement: 60-70% CaO + 20-25% SiO₂ + 5-10% Al₂O₃
hallmarkReactions: Setting of Plaster of Paris: 2(CaSO₄·½H₂O) + 3H₂O --> 2(CaSO₄·2H₂O) (Gypsum matrix)
Limewater milkiness cycle: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ --> CaCO₃↓ + H₂O; CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ --> Ca(HCO₃)₂
Slaking of lime: CaO + H₂O --> Ca(OH)₂ (ΔH = -65 kJ/mol, violent hissing)
examQuickRule: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O; POP is CaSO₄·½H₂O; dead burnt plaster is anhydrous CaSO₄.

name: Scandium
highYieldNote: Sc is a transition element because Sc atom has 3d¹; but Sc³⁺ is colorless and diamagnetic (3d⁰). Only forms Sc³⁺ (d⁰ configuration). Sc³⁺ salts are completely colorless and diamagnetic, yet Scandium is classified as a transition element.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2074] Why is Scandium (Z=21) classified as a transition element while Zinc (Z=30) is not? (Ans: IUPAC defines transition metals as elements possessing incompletely filled d-subshells in ground state or in common oxidation states. Scandium atom has 3d¹ (partially filled), whereas Zinc has 3d¹⁰ in both atom and Zn²⁺ ion).

[NEB 2075] Why are Sc³⁺ salts completely colorless and diamagnetic? (Ans: Sc³⁺ loses all 3 valence electrons [Ar] 3d⁰ 4s⁰; having zero d-electrons, d-d transitions are impossible and there are no unpaired electrons).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Scandium shows ONLY a +3 oxidation state in its compounds; +1 and +2 are virtually non-existent because sum of 1st, 2nd, and 3rd ionization energies is compensated by high lattice/hydration enthalpy.
TRAP: Sc³⁺ is isoelectronic with Argon [Ar] 3d⁰.
keyOresAndCompounds: Thortveitite: (Sc,Y)₂Si₂O₇ (scandium silicate)
Scandium Oxide: Sc₂O₃ (amphoteric transition oxide)
Al-Sc Alloys: Used in aerospace frames and high-performance bicycle frames
hallmarkReactions: Oxidation of Scandium: 4Sc + 3O₂ --> 2Sc₂O₃
Reaction with acids: 2Sc + 6HCl --> 2ScCl₃ + 3H₂↑
examQuickRule: Sc is a transition element because Sc atom has 3d¹; but Sc³⁺ is colorless and diamagnetic (3d⁰).

name: Titanium
highYieldNote: Ti⁴⁺ is colorless (3d⁰); Ti³⁺ is purple (3d¹). Reduced via Kroll process using Mg in Argon. Space-age metal: high strength-to-weight ratio and corrosion resistance. TiO₂ is the premier non-toxic white pigment.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2077] Why is Titanium referred to as a strategic or space-age metal? (Ans: High strength-to-weight ratio, exceptional corrosion resistance due to passive oxide film, and ability to withstand extreme temperatures without losing structural integrity).

[NEB 2073] Why is Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) widely used as a white pigment instead of White Lead? (Ans: High refractive index (2.7) provides high opacity and brightness, is completely non-toxic, and does not turn black when exposed to atmospheric H₂S, unlike lead pigments).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Kroll Process: Titanium cannot be reduced by carbon (forms brittle titanium carbide TiC); it must be reduced by molten Magnesium in an inert Argon atmosphere at 1073 K: TiCl₄ + 2Mg --> Ti + 2MgCl₂.
TRAP: Ti⁴⁺ compounds are colorless and diamagnetic (3d⁰), whereas Ti³⁺ compounds (3d¹) are purple/violet due to d-d transition.
keyOresAndCompounds: Ilmenite: FeTiO₃; Rutile: TiO₂
Titanium Tetrachloride: TiCl₄ (volatile covalent liquid that fumes in moist air to produce white smoke screens of TiO₂·H₂O and HCl)
Ziegler-Natta Catalyst: TiCl₄ + Al(C₂H₅)₃ (used in stereospecific polymerization of ethene)
hallmarkReactions: Kroll Process reduction: TiCl₄ + 2Mg --[Ar atmosphere, 1073 K]--> Ti(s) + 2MgCl₂
Fuming in air: TiCl₄ + 2H₂O --> TiO₂ + 4HCl↑ (smoke-screen generator)
examQuickRule: Ti⁴⁺ is colorless (3d⁰); Ti³⁺ is purple (3d¹). Reduced via Kroll process using Mg in Argon.

name: Vanadium
highYieldNote: V colors: +5 Yellow (VO₂⁺), +4 Blue (VO²⁺), +3 Green (V³⁺), +2 Violet (V²⁺). V₂O₅ is Contact catalyst. Displays 4 distinct colored oxidation states: V²⁺ (violet), V³⁺ (green), VO²⁺ (+4, blue), VO₂⁺ (+5, yellow). V₂O₅ is the catalyst in the Contact Process.
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2078, 2074] Why does Vanadium exhibit variable oxidation states and distinct solution colors? (Ans: Close energetic proximity of 3d³ and 4s² orbitals allows loss of 2, 3, 4, or 5 electrons. Solutions show vivid colors: V²⁺ (violet), V³⁺ (green), VO²⁺ (+4, blue), VO₂⁺ (+5, yellow)).

[NEB 2076] Explain the catalytic role of V₂O₅ in the Contact Process for sulfuric acid. (Ans: Acts via variable oxidation state: V₂O₅ oxidizes SO₂ to SO₃ while reducing to V₂O₄; atmospheric O₂ then re-oxidizes V₂O₄ back to V₂O₅).
futureExamTraps: TRAP: Vanadium Redox Battery uses four oxidation states of vanadium (V²⁺/V³⁺ at anode, VO²⁺/VO₂⁺ at cathode) to store grid electrical energy without cross-contamination!
TRAP: V₂O₅ is AMPHOTERIC: dissolves in strong acids to give dioxovanadium(V) VO₂⁺, and in alkalis to give orthovanadate VO₄³⁻.
keyOresAndCompounds: Vanadinite: Pb₅(VO₄)₃Cl; Patronite: VS₄
Vanadium Pentoxide: V₂O₅ (industrial Contact process catalyst)
Ferrovanadium: Master alloy added to steel to produce shock-resistant tools
hallmarkReactions: Contact Process catalytic mechanism: SO₂ + V₂O₅ --> SO₃ + V₂O₄; 2V₂O₄ + O₂ --> 2V₂O₅
Amphoteric dissolution: V₂O₅ + 6NaOH --> 2Na₃VO₄ (Sodium vanadate) + 3H₂O
Reduction ladder with Zinc: VO₂⁺ (yellow) --> VO²⁺ (blue) --> V³⁺ (green) --> V²⁺ (violet)
examQuickRule: V colors: +5 Yellow (VO₂⁺), +4 Blue (VO²⁺), +3 Green (V³⁺), +2 Violet (V²⁺). V₂O₅ is Contact catalyst.

name: Chromium
highYieldNote: Chromium is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. Chromyl chloride test yields red CrO₂Cl₂ fumes. Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ ⇌ Yellow CrO₄²⁻. Anomalous half-filled 3d⁵ 4s¹ configuration (exchange energy stability). Cr(VI) in K₂Cr₂O₇ is a powerful oxidizer; Cr³⁺ is green.
nebGradeLevel: Grade 12 Core (3d Transition Metals & Heavy Metallurgy)
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2076] Write the electronic configuration of Chromium (Z=24) and explain why it is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ instead of [Ar] 3d⁴ 4s². (Ans: Symmetrical spherical distribution and maximum exchange energy of the exactly half-filled 3d⁵ subshell impart exceptional thermodynamic stability).

[NEB 2078, 2073] What is the Chromyl Chloride test? Give the balanced equation and observation. (Ans: Specific test for ionic chlorides: chloride salt + solid K₂Cr₂O₇ + conc. H₂SO₄ heated yields deep red-orange vapors of chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂); vapors passed into NaOH give yellow Na₂CrO₄, which turns into yellow PbCrO₄ precipitate with lead acetate).

[NEB 2075] Why does acidified Potassium Dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) change color from orange to green on passing SO₂ gas? (Ans: Dichromate is reduced from orange Cr(VI) to green Cr³⁺: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3SO₂ + 2H⁺ --> 2Cr³⁺(green) + 3SO₄²⁻ + H₂O).

pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2077, 2074] What is Lanthanide Contraction? Explain its two fundamental causes and three major chemical consequences. (Ans: The steady, continuous decrease in atomic and ionic radii of elements from Lanthanum (₅₇La) to Lutetium (₇₁Lu). Causes: 1. Progressive increase in nuclear charge (+1 per element). 2. Imperfect shielding of 4f electrons due to their diffuse, scattered spatial distribution. Consequences: 1. Atomic radii of 4d and 5d transition pairs (e.g., Zr=160 pm and Hf=159 pm) are almost identical. 2. Basicity of hydroxides decreases steadily from La(OH)₃ (most basic) to Lu(OH)₃ (least basic). 3. Chemical separation of lanthanides is difficult due to identical properties).

[NEB 2076] Why is Lu(OH)₃ the least basic hydroxide among all Lanthanides? (Ans: According to Fajans' rule, as the ionic radius decreases from La³⁺ (106 pm) to Lu³⁺ (85 pm), the polarizing power increases; this increases the covalent character of the Lu-O bond, making cleavage to release OH⁻ most difficult).

highYieldNote: Calomel (Hg₂Cl₂) = insoluble & non-toxic; Corrosive sublimate (HgCl₂) = soluble & lethal. Hg stored in Iron. Nessler's detects NH₃. VOLATILE METAL (Group 12). pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2077, 2074] Why is Mercury the ONLY metal that is liquid at standard room temperature? (Ans: 1. Completely filled 5d¹⁰ 6s² electronic configuration provides no unpaired electrons for inter-atomic metallic bonding. 2. Relativistic 6s contraction tightly binds the 6s² electron pair to the nucleus, preventing valence orbital overlap between adjacent Hg atoms).

[NEB 2078, 2075] What is the 'Tailing of Mercury'? How does Ozone cause it, and how is the meniscus restored? (Ans: Pure mercury does not wet glass and forms a convex meniscus. When exposed to Ozone (O₃), it oxidizes to mercurous oxide (Hg₂O) which dissolves in mercury, causing it to lose its meniscus and leave a tail-like trail on glass walls: 2Hg + O₃ --> Hg₂O + O₂. Restored by shaking vigorously with water, which hydrolyzes/removes Hg₂O).

[NEB 2077, 2073] Why can liquid Mercury be safely stored and transported in an Iron container, but not in containers of Copper, Silver, or Gold? (Ans: Mercury forms amalgams with almost all metals (Cu, Ag, Au, Al, Na) by metallic solution, dissolving their walls; Iron (Fe), Platinum (Pt), and Tungsten (W) do not form amalgams with mercury).

[NEB 2076, 2072] Differentiate between Calomel (Hg₂Cl₂) and Corrosive Sublimate (HgCl₂) in terms of solubility, toxicity, and chemical formula. (Ans: 1. CALOMEL: Hg₂Cl₂ (dimeric with Hg-Hg bond [⁺Hg-Hg⁺]), INSOLUBLE in water, NON-TOXIC (used in medicine as purgative and in standard calomel reference electrodes). 2. CORROSIVE SUBLIMATE: HgCl₂ (covalent linear molecule), FREELY SOLUBLE in water and alcohol, LETHALLY POISONOUS).

[NEB 2075, 2071] What is Nessler's Reagent? Write the reaction and product formed when it reacts with Ammonia gas. (Ans: Nessler's Reagent is an alkaline solution of Potassium Tetraiodomercurate(II) (K₂[HgI₄] in KOH). Reacts with ammonia to form an intense brown precipitate of Iodide of Millon's Base: 2K₂[HgI₄] + NH₃ + 3KOH --> [O-Hg₂-NH₂]I↓ (brown ppt) + 7KI + 2H₂O. Used as a sensitive confirmatory test for NH₄⁺/NH₃).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP: Calomel vs Corrosive Sublimate: In Calomel, mercury is in the +1 oxidation state (Hg₂²⁺ dimer, ⁺Hg-Hg⁺, diamagnetic). In Corrosive Sublimate, mercury is in the +2 oxidation state (Hg²⁺). Swapping their toxicities or formulas is a fatal exam mistake!

nebGradeLevel: Grade 11 & 12 Core (Group 14 Heavy Metals & Inert Pair Effect)
pastExamQuestions: [NEB 2079, 2076] What is Plumbosolvency? Why are lead pipes unsafe for carrying soft water but safe for hard water? (Ans: Plumbosolvency is the property of lead dissolving in soft water containing dissolved oxygen to form soluble, toxic lead hydroxide: 2Pb + O₂ + 2H₂O --> 2Pb(OH)₂. In hard water containing calcium carbonates and sulfates, a protective, insoluble crust of PbCO₃ and PbSO₄ precipitates inside the pipe, preventing lead poisoning).

[NEB 2078, 2074] Explain why Pb(IV) compounds act as powerful oxidizing agents while Pb(II) compounds are stable. (Ans: Inert Pair Effect: The reluctance of the outer 6s² electron pair to unpair and participate in bonding due to poor shielding by intervening 4f¹⁴ and 5d¹⁰ subshells. Consequently, Pb²⁺ is the stable ground state, and Pb(IV) in PbO₂ or PbCl₄ eagerly gains 2 electrons to reduce to Pb²⁺).

[NEB 2075] What happens when Lead Nitrate crystals are heated strongly? Write the balanced chemical equation. (Ans: Decomposes with crackling sound (decrepitation), leaving a yellow-brown residue of litharge (PbO) and releasing reddish-brown NO₂ gas and O₂: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ --[Δ]--> 2PbO (yellow) + 4NO₂↑ (brown fumes) + O₂↑).
futureExamTraps: FATAL TRAP in Halide Stability: PbCl₄ exists (covalent liquid, decomposes to PbCl₂ + Cl₂ on warming), but PbI₄ and PbBr₄ do NOT exist! The strongly oxidizing Pb⁴⁺ immediately oxidizes I⁻ to I₂: Pb⁴⁺ + 2I⁻ --> Pb²⁺ + I₂!
